group.passage:
Chess is one of the oldest strategy games still played today, yet the version found in parks and phone apps is the product of many centuries of change. The game is generally believed to have begun in India around 1,500 years ago. Its pieces [[1]] the army of that era, which went into battle with foot soldiers, horsemen, elephants, and chariots led by a king and his chief adviser. In other words, the board was a small copy of a real battlefield.
From India, the game moved west into Persia and then across the Arab world, where it [[2]] among scholars and rulers alike. Around a thousand years ago, it reached Europe, and there its pieces were gradually reshaped to suit local tastes. The elephant turned into the bishop, and the king’s male adviser [[3]] the queen, a figure far more common at European courts.
For centuries, however, the queen remained one of the weakest pieces, able to move only one square diagonally at a time. That changed in the late fifteenth century, when she was granted [[4]] new powers that let her travel any distance in a straight line or along a diagonal. Games that had once dragged on for hours became sharper, and the [[5]] of play quickened as attacks could now come from across the board. Even the [[6]] pawn, the least valuable piece, gained importance, since one that reached the far side could now become this mighty queen.
Another turning point came in 1997, when an IBM computer called Deep Blue narrowly [[7]] world champion Garry Kasparov in a six-game contest, becoming the first machine to defeat a reigning champion in a full series of games. The result sparked [[8]] disagreement over whether machines could ever truly think. Today, many experts regard it as a [[9]] in the history of computing rather than a defeat for humanity. A free phone app now plays far better than any person, and even the best human player would prove no [[10]] for a program running on an ordinary laptop.

translation_zh.text:
西洋棋是至今仍有人在玩的最古老策略遊戲之一，然而我們在公園裡和手機應用程式上看到的版本，是歷經許多世紀演變的產物。一般認為這種遊戲大約在1500年前起源於印度。它的棋子仿照當時的軍隊：那時的軍隊帶著步兵、騎兵、象和戰車上陣，由國王和他的首席謀臣率領。換句話說，棋盤就是真實戰場的縮小版。
這種遊戲從印度向西傳入波斯，再傳遍阿拉伯世界，在學者和統治者之間都十分興盛。大約一千年前，它傳到歐洲，棋子在那裡逐漸被改造，以迎合當地的喜好。象變成了主教，國王的男性謀臣則讓位給皇后，因為在歐洲宮廷中，皇后是常見得多的人物。
然而，好幾個世紀以來，皇后一直是最弱的棋子之一，一次只能斜走一格。到了十五世紀末情況改變了：她獲得了全面的新權力，可以沿直線或斜線走任意距離。原本拖上好幾個小時的棋局變得更犀利，下棋的節奏也加快了，因為攻擊現在可以從棋盤的另一端發動。就連地位低下的兵——價值最低的棋子——也變得重要起來，因為走到對面底線的兵，現在可以變成這位強大的皇后。
另一個轉捩點出現在1997年：一部名為「深藍」的IBM電腦在一場六盤的對戰中以些微差距擊敗世界冠軍卡斯帕洛夫，成為第一部在完整系列對局中擊敗衛冕世界冠軍的機器。這個結果引發了激烈的爭論：機器到底能不能真正思考？如今，許多專家把它視為電腦發展史上的里程碑，而不是人類的失敗。現在一個免費的手機應用程式下得比任何人都好，即使是最強的人類棋手，也不是一台普通筆電上執行的程式的對手。
